scenarios.name: converge
scenarios.topic: Should companies adopt fully remote work?
scenarios.evidence_seed:
Remote work has been shown to increase productivity for knowledge workers by 13%.
Communication overhead increases by approximately 30% in fully remote teams.

payload.content: Evidence indicates remote work reliably raises individual productivity, driven by quieter work environments and fewer sick days across large employee samples.
payload.evidence_summary: Two large-sample studies agree on direction.

payload.content: The productivity figure comes from knowledge workers only, so generalising it to all roles overstates the case and hides coordination costs.
payload.reasoning: Scope of the cited samples is narrower than the claim asserts.

payload.content: Treat the office as an intermittently scheduled collaboration venue rather than a daily default, letting teams reserve dense weeks for coordination-heavy work.
payload.novelty_rationale: Reframes the office as a scheduling primitive, not a location.

payload.content: Remote work raises individual throughput while raising coordination cost; the defensible position is a scheduled hybrid where focus work is remote and coordination is co-located.
resolved_tensions: Individual output versus coordination cost, resolved as scoped.
